scopeReview: PSO-5.E.1–3: global agricultural chains, commodity-export dependence, political relationships, infrastructure and trade patterns. Food availability and household access are separated; risks and benefits remain conditional rather than uniformly pro- or anti-trade.
varietyReview: Four meaningful original stimuli: cross-border staged product map, export-price-shock table, signed grain-flow chart and landed-cost offers. Deterministic checks trace directions, compute shock exposure, balance one grain and add price/freight/duty. Remaining cases apply resilience, seasonality and multiscale transmission.
repetitionReview: Unlike5.7 domestic chain organization, this set emphasizes cross-border dependence, sourcing conditions and trade shocks. Four distinct evidence tasks, not country-name substitutions. All data invented; varied keys and detailed option reasoning, difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Official scope and FAO research themes checked; no current tariff, actual national export statistic, third-party question or trade map copied. All assumptions explicit; no new resources or human-review claim.

questions.correctOption: Growing, processing and final consumption can occur in different countries linked by trade.
questions.independentReview: Verified the A→B beans and B→C processed-product routes and distinct territorial polygons. All three countries are invented; no claim about actual cocoa-country trade patterns, revenue shares or unequal treatment is inferred solely from arrows.

Independently computed coffee shares80% and20%, multiplied by25% to obtain20% and5%. Postshock totals80 and190 million. Distinct denominators avoid conflating absolute revenue losses20/10 with percentage losses.

Independently balanced80+40=120 entering;10+20=30 leaving;90 remaining. Same grain, same year and explicit no-stock/no-other-use assumption prevent mixed-product or hidden allocation ambiguity. Not a nutritional adequacy measure.

questions.correctOption: Far:120 units/tonne, despite its higher freight cost.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed140 versus120, a20-unit difference. Duty is explicitly fixed units/tonne rather than a percentage, so there is no disputed tax base. No legal or actual-country tariff claim.

questions.correctOption: Lower export earnings can reduce purchasing capacity for imports and transmit pressure through the wider economy.
questions.independentReview: Cross-checked FAO commodity-dependence research for possible macroeconomic shock transmission. No exact exchange-rate response, welfare estimate or uniform country outcome assumed.

questions.correctOption: Both routes share a bottleneck, so disruption at that facility could affect both despite different origins.
questions.independentReview: Checked common-node logic rather than treating all trade diversification as ineffective. Conditional facility disruption, not a fabricated real crisis or forecast.

questions.correctOption: Complementary seasonal production and transport links can connect supply in one region with demand in another.
questions.independentReview: Used a hypothetical suitable season rather than claiming all opposite-hemisphere crops share one harvest calendar. No actual shipment, footprint or current price invented.

questions.correctOption: High export tonnage alone proves that every resident is food secure.
questions.independentReview: Checked the answer targets an inference to avoid rather than condemning all export farming. No causal direction is inferred from coexistence of exports and unmet access.

questions.correctOption: One trade barrier is reduced, while remaining infrastructure limits may still constrain reliable perishable-food delivery.
questions.independentReview: Aligned political/infrastructure mechanisms with PSO-5.E.3. Hypothetical procedural change, not current law or a claim that refrigeration is required for every food.

questions.correctOption: Alternative suppliers’ usable capacity, prices, shipping access and compatibility with domestic handling requirements.
questions.independentReview: Selected evidence needed for a conditional resilience claim without inventing actual exporter capacity or using current political events. Production is distinguished from grain available for export.

questions.correctOption: Interdependence links a production-region shock with consumption and trade conditions elsewhere.
questions.independentReview: Consistent with FAO trade-shock framework; no particular real drought, country, food-price increase or guaranteed impact magnitude claimed.
